correctness.rationale: For alpha_i,delta_i>0 and beta_{j->i}>=0, all single-spin flips are possible and the finite CTMC is irreducible. The 4-configuration Kolmogorov products cancel constant recovery. At A=empty, alpha_i beta_{i->j}=alpha_j beta_{j->i}, forcing paired directed edges; setting t_ij=beta_{i->j}/alpha_j makes t symmetric. For t_ij>0, the same square with A={k} forces t_ki=t_kj for all distinct k. Therefore positive components are complete and by triangle propagation have one t-value kappa_C, with 2-site case immediate. Conversely the proposed w(A) gives w(A+i)/w(A)=alpha_i(1+kappa_C |A∩C|)/delta_i on every birth, hence detailed balance and normalized unique stationary law. Summing over infected count yields elementary-symmetric normalizer; uniform components correspond bijectively to set partitions. A 3-path four-state square has product difference beta^2>0. Independent exact checker verified canonical assigned Git tree, all 1099 labeled graphs n<=5 with expected Bell counts 1,2,5,15,52 and 18,801 squares, and an independent 7-site heterogeneous directed example with 448 detailed-balance equations and exact normalizer 233218301/404250. This finite evidence corroborates, not replaces, the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: A complete structural classification of the exact stationary reversibility boundary for the natural positive-immigration additive SIS process, including heterogeneous directed rates, is a worthwhile and motivated mathematical question. It identifies exactly which contact topologies and rate ratios permit a potential/detailed-balance description, constructs explicit stationary weights and quadratic-time component normalization, and supplies the sharp positive-rate minimal graph obstruction. It differs substantively from approximate mean-field steady states and known complete-graph special cases; its importance does not depend on a paper-sized general theorem. The small-path example itself is elementary, but anchors the all-n classification rather than claiming a cheap isolated negative result.
